rationale.conceptual: The method involves a custom combination of several established techniques (vdW-DFT, DFPT, Wannier interpolation, anisotropic Migdal-Eliashberg) to compute superconducting Tc. Reproducing the results requires a solid grasp of the underlying theory, proper selection of functionals and pseudopotentials, and careful handling of convergence parameters; it is not a mere textbook application.
rationale.execution: The pipeline consists of multiple interdependent steps (geometry relaxation, phonon calculations, Wannierization, EPW aME solution) across five different crystal structures, each requiring careful input generation and file handoffs. Orchestrating Quantum ESPRESSO, EPW, and Wannier90 in a HPC environment is non-trivial.

difficulty.reasoning: The task requires running a complex first-principles superconductivity prediction workflow (DFT relaxation, phonon DFPT, Wannier interpolation, anisotropic Migdal-Eliashberg) using multiple specialized codes, demanding both conceptual understanding of electron-phonon coupling and orchestration of a multi-stage HPC pipeline.

compute_estimate.reasoning: DFT and DFPT calculations on moderate-sized supercells, plus dense-k/q-grid EPW interpolations, require substantial CPU memory (tens to hundreds of GB) as typical for first-principles superconductivity studies on HPC clusters.
